proof_summary: Counting pairs whose gcd is divisible by each \(p^i\) gives numerator valuation \(\sum_{i\ge1}\lfloor N/p^i\rfloor^2\), while Legendre’s formula gives denominator valuation \(\sum_{i\ge1}S(\lfloor N/p^i\rfloor)\), with \(S(q)=\sum_{j=1}^q j\lfloor q/j\rfloor\); the bound \(S(q)\le q^2\) also establishes exact divisibility. For \(N=np+k\) with \(0\le k<p\), every \(\lfloor N/p^i\rfloor\) for \(i\ge1\) equals \(\lfloor np/p^i\rfloor\), so the resulting valuation differences are identical.
